title: Burrell to George, One Second Left
dek: Down 70-69 with one second left and the length of the floor to go, UConn won on Scott Burrell's overhand pass and Tate George's turnaround jumper.

setup.text: UConn came to the Meadowlands as the No. 1 seed in the East, 30-5 and ranked third. Jim Calhoun's Huskies had already won a share of the Big East regular-season title and the Big East tournament, then beaten Boston University and California in Hartford to reach the regional semifinals.

Clemson, the No. 5 seed and No. 17 in the AP poll, arrived 26-8 under coach Cliff Ellis, built around big men Dale Davis and Elden Campbell, a 6-foot-11 senior. The Tigers had trailed La Salle by 19 points in the first half of their second-round game before rallying to win, 79-75.

A win would put UConn in a regional final for only the second time in school history, and the first since 1964. Calhoun knew how this kind of night could end: in 1984, coaching Northeastern, he had lost a first-round NCAA game in this same arena, 70-69, on a last-second shot by Virginia Commonwealth.

story.text: UConn's full-court press owned the first half. Clemson turned the ball over 16 times and was whistled for two 10-second violations before the break, and the Huskies led 38-29.

Chris Smith scored eight points in the first six minutes of the second half, and with 12:36 left UConn led 59-40. Smith finished with 23 points; Scott Burrell, a freshman forward, pulled down 15 rebounds.

Then Clemson turned the game around. The Tigers went to a press of their own, made six straight shots during one stretch and gave the ball away only four times after halftime. UConn, meanwhile, did not make a field goal after the 6:03 mark until the final second.
A 25-8 Clemson run cut a 19-point lead to two with 3:38 left. The Huskies, whose press had forced opponents into about 22 turnovers a game all season, were suddenly the ones making mistakes.

sequence.text: A 25-8 Clemson run, sparked by the Tigers' own press, has cut a 19-point deficit to two.

Pressured by Derrick Forrest, Tate George loses the ball out of bounds in the backcourt, UConn's 19th turnover. Possession first goes to UConn, but after official James Stupin confers with Jim Bain, Clemson gets the ball.
David Young, a sophomore who had taken only one shot all night and missed it, is left open on the left side and hits a 3-pointer. It is Clemson's first lead since the opening minutes.
Out of a UConn timeout, George misses a jumper from the top of the key.
Sean Tyson grabs the rebound and is fouled by Burrell. Clemson is in the bonus.

Tyson misses the front end of the one-and-one. Burrell rebounds and UConn calls its last timeout with one second showing; Clemson answers with a timeout and Ellis puts the 6-foot-11 Campbell, arms raised, in front of the inbounder.

UConn runs a practice play called "home run." Burrell, a pitcher who had turned down more than $100,000 from the Seattle Mariners, throws an overhand pass of more than 80 feet. George catches it near the right corner, Tyson backs off to avoid fouling, and George turns and shoots from about 16 feet. A CBS slow-motion review showed the clock passing from one-tenth to zero as he released; the horn sounded with the ball in the air.

quotes.text: I just never thought we'd have enough time to do it.
The surprising thing was, when I turned, he backed off.
I never really thought we were going to lose.

aftermath.text: Back in Storrs, about 2,000 fans who had watched on a big screen at the new Gampel Pavilion ran onto the floor, and students lit a bonfire outside the dormitory complex known as the Jungle.

Two nights later, in the same building, UConn led Duke 78-77 in the closing seconds of overtime when George stepped in front of a Bobby Hurley pass. The ball slipped through his hands and out of bounds, and Duke called timeout with 2.6 seconds left.

Mike Krzyzewski saw that no one was guarding Christian Laettner on the inbound and called "Special." Laettner threw the ball to Brian Davis, took it right back and hit a double-clutch 14-footer at the buzzer: Duke 79, UConn 78.

UConn's season ended at 31-6, the same way its 1964 tournament run had ended: with a loss to Duke in a regional final. Calhoun said afterward that he would not trade his players for 100 Final Fours. George and Smith made the East Regional all-tournament team, and Calhoun was the Big East's coach of the year.

legacy.text: To UConn fans the play is known simply as "The Shot." Eight years later, a Tacoma News Tribune story on another UConn buzzer-beater credited George's basket with instantly marking UConn as a national force.
When Richard Hamilton beat Washington at the buzzer in the 1998 East Regional semifinals, the Associated Press game story recalled Burrell's pass and George's jumper.
Both men on the play reached the NBA: George went to the New Jersey Nets with the 22nd pick of the 1990 draft, and Burrell to the Charlotte Hornets at No. 20 in 1993.
